LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare --printsrcinfo`.

The `source` array downloads a tarball from the project's own upstream repository (`https://github.com/YourDoritos/pVPN/archive/v${pkgver}.tar.gz`), which is standard packaging practice. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is acceptable for this gate per the audit instructions.

At the top level / global scope, the PKGBUILD only defines standard variables (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.) and function bodies for `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()`. There is no `pkgver()` function and no command substitution or executable statements at the top level that would run during sourcing. The `_srcdir="pVPN-${pkgver}"` assignment is a benign string concatenation.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions contain code (Go module downloads, `chmod -R u+w`, `install` commands) but these will not execute under `--nobuild --noprepare`. They are out of scope for this gate and will be reviewed in the full PKGBUILD audit.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD; top-level scope benign for narrow gate.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a Go-based application. The source is fetched from the package's own declared upstream (`github.com/YourDoritos/pVPN`) via a normal `source=` array with `SKIP` checksum (a standard VCS/practical pattern, not malicious). The build process uses ordinary Go toolchain flags (`-buildmode=pie`, `-trimpath`, `-mod=readonly`, `-ldflags="-s -w"`) and installs three built binaries into `$pkgdir/usr/bin/`, a patched systemd unit, and the LICENSE file. The `chmod -R u+w` on the local gopath is clearly explained as a workaround for Go toolchain bootstrap permission issues affecting downstream package managers like yay — not a malicious action.

No red flags are present: no obfuscated commands, no base64 blobs, no `eval`, no `curl|sh`, no data exfiltration to unexpected hosts, no modifications to files outside the package scope. The upstream URL points to a personal GitHub account rather than the official Proton VPN organization, which is a hygiene/trust consideration (third-party fork or reimplementation), but the PKGBUILD itself only fetches and builds what its own `source` declares, which is normal AUR behavior. Functionality within the upstream tarball is outside the scope of this PKGBUILD audit.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard Go AUR package, no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for pvpn-go.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard Arch Linux pacman `.install` hook script for the pvpn-go package. It performs routine post-installation tasks typical of daemon packages: creating a system group, setting up restricted-permission directories (`/etc/pvpn`, `/var/lib/pvpn` with mode 0750/0660), migrating legacy user-home configs to system locations, enabling the systemd service, and cleaning up on removal. The `eval echo "~${_user}"` pattern is a common legitimate shell idiom for expanding tilde notation to a home directory, with `_user` safely derived from `SUDO_USER` or `logname`. No network requests, obfuscated code, credential exfiltration, or unexpected system modifications are present. All operations are consistent with standard AUR daemon packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR daemon install script; no malicious activity detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for pvpn-go.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard Arch Linux `.install` script for the pvpn-go package. It performs routine post-installation, post-upgrade, and pre/post-removal tasks typical for a VPN client that runs a daemon:

- Creates a `pvpn` system group and directories (`/etc/pvpn`, `/var/lib/pvpn`) with mode 0750/0660
- Migrates config/session files from old user-home paths to system paths on upgrade
- Enables and starts the `pvpnd` systemd service
- Cleans up on removal

The `eval echo "~${_user}"` idiom is standard shell practice for tilde expansion when the username is stored in a variable; `$_user` is derived from `SUDO_USER` or `logname`, not arbitrary user input. No network requests, no downloads, no obfuscation, and no operations outside the package's own scope are present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
